title: The Late Enrollment Penalty Charged on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Plan
content:
A member who went without Part D or other creditable drug coverage after their initial enrollment period pays a late enrollment penalty for as long as they hold Part D coverage under a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan.

The monthly penalty is the late enrollment penalty rate applied to the national base beneficiary premium for the contract year, multiplied by the number of months CMS has counted without creditable coverage, and rounded on the rounding basis of the plan held.

## The evidence of earlier coverage

The evidence of earlier creditable drug coverage held on the enrollment intake is a certificate of creditable coverage on file, or coverage verified with the prior carrier. Where that evidence is on file the plan sends a reconsideration to CMS. The member's own statement that they had drug coverage starts that enquiry but never removes the penalty by itself.

## Two circumstances that end or reset the penalty

1. A member who becomes eligible for the low-income subsidy stops owing the penalty from the month the subsidy begins, and any penalty already charged for those months is removed.
2. A member who reaches 65 and had the penalty applied while under 65 on a disability entitlement has the count reset to zero from the month they turn 65.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses of this policy are **no longer in force** and are set out here only so that they are not applied:

1. "the penalty is removed and every month of it credited back once CMS confirms the earlier coverage was creditable" — no longer in force.
2. "The count of months is CMS's, not the plan's: the plan bills what CMS supplies and never adds or removes a month on its own view of the member's history." — no longer in force.
